options: Directs SQL Server to reuse one specific, already-captured plan_id for a query_id, overriding normal cost-based plan selection
Deletes all other plans for that query from Query Store
Only suggests a plan to the optimizer, which may still choose a different one
Rebuilds indexes used by that query
questions.explain: Plan forcing is a directive, not a hint — SQL Server uses the forced plan instead of compiling a new one, unless the forced plan becomes unusable.

questions.q: How can you tell whether a forced plan is actually succeeding in applying, per this lesson?
options: Check is_forced_plan and last_force_failure_reason_desc on sys.query_store_plan
There is no way to check this
Run DBCC CHECKDB
Check sys.dm_os_wait_stats
questions.explain: last_force_failure_reason_desc reveals silent forcing failures, such as a forced plan that depended on an index that was later dropped.

questions.q: How does Query Store plan forcing differ from a plan guide, per this lesson?
options: Plan forcing reuses an already-captured real plan and is tied to Query Store; a plan guide attaches hints to a query pattern independent of Query Store and is more flexible but more work to set up
They are functionally identical in every way
Plan guides only work in Azure SQL Database
Plan forcing requires modifying the application's query text, plan guides never do
questions.explain: Plan forcing points at a real captured plan and is easy to audit through Query Store views; plan guides can attach any hint but require matching query text patterns.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when does forcing a plan become a 'band-aid' rather than a legitimate fix?
options: When it's used instead of fixing the real cause of plan instability, like missing statistics or an index gap, and the underlying data keeps changing without the forced plan adapting
Whenever it's used at all, since forcing is never appropriate
Only when used on a query with fewer than 100 executions
Only when used with sp_query_store_unforce_plan
questions.explain: A forced plan doesn't adapt as data grows — forcing without addressing the root cause can leave a stale plan in place long after it stops being the right one.

questions.q: How do you release a previously forced plan?
options: EXEC sys.sp_query_store_unforce_plan with the same @query_id and @plan_id
ALTER DATABASE SET QUERY_STORE = OFF
DBCC FREEPROCCACHE
DROP INDEX on the query's underlying table
questions.explain: sp_query_store_unforce_plan is the direct counterpart to sp_query_store_force_plan, releasing the forced plan for that query.
